Container.Name: CommunityEvents-v2-Prod
Container.Overview: CommunityEvents v2 — PRODUCTION container. Tracks the :v2-prod image tag, which is never built: scripts/promote-v2-prod.sh retags the :v2-stage digest that was tested, so what runs here is byte-identical to what passed stage. Hosts every production community as a tenant of one deployment; its own root tenant serves the CommunityEvents landing page, and DinnerBears is a non-root tenant on its own domain. Points at the communityevents database, separate from stage's communityevents_stage and from v1's dinnerbears.

Config.Name: Web Port
Config.Description: Host port for the production web interface. 20020 is this project's allocated prod port — see ../PORTS.md, project 02, 20PP0. Take a new port from that file rather than picking one here.

Config.Name: DB Host
Config.Description: MySQL host IP address — the same server that carries stage and v1, a different database

Config.Name: DB Port
Config.Description: MySQL port

Config.Name: DB Name
Config.Description: MySQL database name — the PRODUCTION v2 database. Never dinnerbears (that is v1's, and the import reads it) and never communityevents_stage. This database does not exist until you create it; see docs/NEW_INSTANCE_SETUP.md.

Config.Name: DB User
Config.Description: MySQL username — matches the database name by convention, as stage's does. Grant it on the communityevents database ONLY: a production account that can also reach communityevents_stage or dinnerbears turns a mistyped DB Name into a silent cross-environment write rather than a connection error.

Config.Name: DB Password
Config.Description: MySQL password for the communityevents account — a new one, not stage's

Config.Name: JWT Secret
Config.Description: Secret key for JWT tokens — generate a new one. Do not reuse v1's or stage's: a shared secret would let a token minted on one deployment be accepted by the other. openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: Secret Encryption Key
Config.Description: Encrypts every credential stored in the database (v2-7). Leave EMPTY on this new install and one is generated on first start, written to the App Data volume below -- BACK THAT FILE UP THE MOMENT IT APPEARS. Map App Data before first boot: without it each container recreate generates a fresh key, and the deployment then refuses to start because the database holds secrets encrypted under a key that no longer exists. That is how v2-7's stage deploy produced three keys in three recreates. Set this field only to supply a key an existing database already needs. Generate: openssl rand -base64 32

Config.Name: Retired Encryption Keys
Config.Description: Previous encryption keys, comma-separated, decrypt-only. Leave empty except while rotating — see npm run secrets:rewrap.

Config.Name: JWT Expires In
Config.Description: JWT token expiry

Config.Name: Google Client ID
Config.Description: Google OAuth Client ID for the DEPLOYMENT — used by the root tenant and inherited only by communities on a subdomain of this deployment. A community on its own domain (DinnerBears) must bring its own credentials and does not fall back to this. The authorized redirect URI is APP_URL + /api/v1/auth/google/callback

Config.Name: Google Client Secret
Config.Description: Google OAuth Client Secret for the deployment

Config.Name: Facebook App ID
Config.Description: Facebook App ID — leave unset to hide the Facebook login button

Config.Name: Facebook App Secret
Config.Description: Facebook App Secret

Config.Name: Brevo API Key
Config.Description: Brevo API key for the DEPLOYMENT's own mail — same inheritance rule as Google above, with one difference that matters: a community on its own domain has NO email fallback at all, which is fatal rather than cosmetic, because registration, verification and password resets are all mail

Config.Name: Brevo From Email
Config.Description: From address for outbound emails from the deployment itself

Config.Name: Brevo From Name
Config.Description: Display name on the deployment's own outbound mail. Defaults to CommunityEvents in code if unset, which is right for the root tenant here.

Config.Name: Resend API Key
Config.Description: Resend API key — optional overflow email provider

Config.Name: Resend From Email
Config.Description: Resend overflow from-address

Config.Name: Resend From Name
Config.Description: Resend overflow from-name

Config.Name: Email Suppression Salt
Config.Description: Random salt for email hash suppression. Generate: openssl rand -hex 32

Config.Name: VAPID Public Key
Config.Description: MUST be copied verbatim from v1 DinnerBears' appdata .env, not generated. A fresh key invalidates every existing DinnerBears push subscription with nothing able to restore it. Omitting it disables push silently.

Config.Name: VAPID Private Key
Config.Description: MUST be copied verbatim from v1 DinnerBears' appdata .env, the matching half of the public key above

Config.Name: VAPID Subject
Config.Description: Contact address in the push JWT (mailto: or URL). This one is NOT part of what binds a subscription, so it is free to become a CommunityEvents address rather than v1's — only the two keys must match. Required here because unset disables push just as a missing key does.

Config.Name: Geocoding API Key
Config.Description: Google Geocoding API key

Config.Name: Google Places API Key
Config.Description: Google Places API key (location enrichment)

Config.Name: Anthropic API Key
Config.Description: Optional — powers the admin 'enrich location' helper. Leave unset to disable it

Config.Name: Cloudflare Email Secret
Config.Description: Shared secret validating inbound Cloudflare Email Routing webhook calls (calendar RSVP replies). Production needs its own, and Cloudflare's calendar@ routes must point here rather than at stage's calendar-stage@ — see docs/CUTOVER_PLAN.md, 'Inbound mail'.

Config.Name: Admin Email
Config.Description: Email address granted admin on first login

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: Public URL of this production deployment — the root tenant's own host. Needs its DNS record and an NGINX Proxy Manager entry pointing at the Web Port above before first boot. Note communityevents.com is somebody else's domain and the GitHub repo name carries no 'project'; neither is a typo for this.

Config.Name: Base Domain
Config.Description: Bare APEX domain for derived contact emails — set it EXPLICITLY rather than letting it default. This deployment is served from www., which is below the apex, and a host below the apex normally has no MX record: with no MX a sender falls back to the A record, so replies time out instead of being refused. Not the session cookie scope — v2-6 made that cookie host-only. Never www.

Config.Name: Calendar Organizer Email
Config.Description: Optional override — defaults to calendar@BASE_DOMAIN

Config.Name: Event Organizer Email
Config.Description: Optional override — defaults to noreply@BASE_DOMAIN

Config.Name: Support Email
Config.Description: Optional override — defaults to hello@BASE_DOMAIN

Config.Name: Is Stage
Config.Description: false for this container — stage builds flag themselves in the UI and production must not. This is the ONLY field distinguishing a production container from a stage one at runtime, since both run NODE_ENV=production, so leaving it true puts a stage banner on the live site.

Config.Name: Email Quota Time Zone
Config.Description: IANA zone your Brevo accounts reset their daily send allowance in. The counters on Admin -> Email roll over at midnight in this zone. Leave empty for UTC, which ends the sending day at 8pm Eastern and makes the deployment believe it has a fresh 300 sends while Brevo is still counting the old day.

Config.Name: Legal Entity Name
Config.Description: The company or person operating this deployment, named in the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy every community starts with. Deployment-wide on purpose: one operator runs every community here. Leave empty and each community's legal pages name the community itself, which is right only when the two are the same — on production they are not, since DinnerBears is a tenant rather than the operator.

Config.Name: Uploads
Config.Description: Persistent storage for uploaded photos and files. Separate from v1's dinnerbears/uploads and from stage's — the import COPIES v1's files here rather than sharing them, so size this for DinnerBears' existing uploads.

Config.Name: App Data
Config.Description: Persistent storage for secret-encryption.key AND the .env holding every secret. MUST be mapped before first boot: without it a generated key is lost on every container recreate, and the deployment then refuses to start once any secret is stored under the old one. Back up secret-encryption.key the moment it is generated — losing it makes every stored credential in the production database unrecoverable.

Config.Name: Root Tenant Slug
Config.Description: Slug of the root tenant row bootstrap creates. Reads as cosmetic and is not: a non-person account's address is <local>@<tenant slug>.internal, so the slug is baked into every service account this deployment creates. Changing it afterwards does not rename those accounts, it grows a second set. Decide it before you run bootstrap; 'root' is fine unless a real community wants that slug.

Config.Name: Instance City Name
Config.Description: Required for bootstrap — bootstrap.ts errors out if this is unset. 'Default' for the root tenant, which is the operator's own community rather than a real city.

Config.Name: Instance Brand Name
Config.Description: The root tenant's brand — the operator's own, not a tenant's. Editable later in Admin → Site Settings.

Config.Name: Instance Theme Primary
Config.Description: Optional, #RRGGBB

Config.Name: Instance Theme Accent
Config.Description: Optional, #RRGGBB

Config.Name: Instance Theme Background
Config.Description: Optional, #RRGGBB

Config.Name: Instance Admin Email
Config.Description: Required for bootstrap. The first admin of the ROOT tenant — the account that holds system_admin and can administer every other community, so it is the operator's address rather than a community organiser's. Creating a tenant creates its first admin; without one a community is a dead end, because registration is invite-gated.

Config.Name: Instance Admin Name
Config.Description: Optional — defaults to 'Admin'

Config.Name: Instance Admin Password
Config.Description: Required for bootstrap. Password for the first production admin sign-in. This is a real credential on a live deployment — treat it as one, and change it after first login.

Config.Name: Instance Bootstrap Force
Config.Description: Leave false. Only set true to re-run bootstrap against a database that already holds real members — on production you almost certainly want the safety refusal.
